source.name: When the focused control inside a focus trap removes itself, focus must stay inside the trap
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/focus-trap/focus-trap/pull/932) at 0eca669477eb3e25c197809efbbbd8fc451eb346. Blind to the maintainers' fix fce60b3a737759c6e0e787d3fa1603f2cb86300a; routing auto.

journey.title: Focus stays in the results dialog after Show all removes itself
journey.goal: Activating a control that removes itself keeps keyboard focus inside the trapped dialog

functionalJourney.title: Show all results with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, lists every result and closes

guards.title: Escape closes results and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: When the 'Show all 4 results' button (#more) is activated, it removes itself from the DOM. This causes the focused element to be deleted, resulting in focus shifting to the <body> and escaping the focus trap.
plan.repair_strategy: After removing the #more button, programmatically move focus to the close button (which remains in the dialog and is focusable) to maintain focus inside the trapped dialog.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus will remain inside the dialog after activating the 'Show all' button, allowing users to continue navigating with Tab or Shift+Tab without escaping the dialog.
functional_risks: The close button must be present and focusable (it is in the current implementation).
If the close button were disabled or hidden, focusing it would fail, but it is neither.
The focus() call may cause a scroll if the close button is not visible, but the dialog is small and the button is in the header.
verification_requirements: After clicking 'Show all 4 results', focus should be on the close button.
Pressing Tab should cycle focus between the close button and itself (since no other focusable elements exist in the dialog), maintaining the trap.
The dialog should remain operable via the close button or Escape key.
